items.title: Cancelling the reconstruction window returns None from the DICOM plugin load()

findings.title: Cancelling the reconstruction window returns None from the DICOM plugin load()
findings.evidence:
image, info = dialog.run()
        if image is None:
            logging.info("Cone-beam reconstruction cancelled by user.")
            return None
findings.explanation: When the user presses Cancel, or when ensureDependencies() fails, the DICOM plugin's load() returns None. Slicer's DICOM browser treats a None return as a failed load and typically reports an error to the user, so a deliberate cancellation is presented as a load failure. The dependency-missing path already shows its own message, so the extra browser error is redundant and confusing.
findings.suggestion: Return a sentinel the browser accepts, or suppress the browser's error for the deliberate-cancel path.

items.title: Good documentation and synthetic tests, but no clinical-use disclaimer

findings.title: Good documentation and synthetic tests, but no clinical-use disclaimer
findings.evidence:
Reconstructs rotational C-arm X-ray runs ("spins", e.g. GE Innova 3D / Siemens DynaCT / Philips XperCT
exports stored as one multi-frame XA or XRF DICOM object) into a 3D volume, straight from Slicer's
DICOM browser.
findings.explanation: The README documents the workflow, the DICOM tags used for geometry, the GE private calibration, the reconstruction methods with literature references, the vendor-orientation troubleshooting steps and how to run the tests, and the module ships a synthetic phantom plus a self test. What is missing is any statement that the output is not validated for clinical use: the module produces HU-like volumes from vendor data and offers no accuracy claim or disclaimer, which matters for a tier-1 tool that will be used on patient studies.
findings.suggestion: Add a short research-use / not-for-clinical-decisions disclaimer and state what validation exists (synthetic phantom only).

findings.title: No research-use or clinical disclaimer for HU-scaled reconstructions
findings.explanation: The module produces Hounsfield-like values from C-arm rotational data, which are only approximate. The README states the DISP caveat and the calibration caveat, but nowhere says that the output is for research and not for diagnosis. Users could take the values as clinically calibrated.
findings.suggestion: Add a short research-use-only statement to the README and the module help text, noting that HU values are approximate and depend on the water value chosen.

items.title: Manual I0 of 0 is silently ignored and replaced by the percentile estimate

findings.title: Manual I0 of 0 is silently ignored and replaced by the percentile estimate
findings.evidence:
if mode == I0_MANUAL and manualValue:
        return float(manualValue)
findings.explanation: A user who selects "Fixed value" and enters 0 (or a value that evaluates falsy) silently falls through to the 99.9th-percentile estimate instead of using the entered value, so the log line "I0 = ..." reports a number the user did not choose. The spin box minimum is 1.0 so 0 is not reachable through the UI, which keeps the practical impact small.
findings.suggestion: Test `manualValue is not None` instead of truthiness.

items.title: Module import inserts its own directory at the front of sys.path

findings.title: Module import inserts its own directory at the front of sys.path
findings.explanation: Importing the module mutates the shared interpreter's sys.path for the whole Slicer session, inserting the module directory at position 0. Any file in that directory would then shadow a stdlib or site-packages module of the same name for every other extension. The directory currently holds only DICOMCBCTRecon.py and DICOMCBCTReconLib/, so the practical risk is low, and Slicer already puts scripted-module directories on sys.path, making this largely redundant.
findings.suggestion: Drop the sys.path manipulation and rely on Slicer's scripted-module path handling, or append instead of insert at position 0.

findings.title: Module folder inserted at the front of sys.path at import time
findings.evidence:
if globals().get("__file__") and _MODULE_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _MODULE_DIR)
findings.explanation: On import the module inserts its own folder at index 0 of sys.path. This is a global side effect in the shared Slicer Python process and affects every later import, including for users who never open the module. The folder contains only this extension's files, so the risk is low, but the insert is not needed when the extension is loaded through Slicer's module paths.
findings.suggestion: Append rather than prepend, or rely on Slicer's module loader, which already adds the module folder when the module is loaded through the CMake build.

items.title: Module-level loadable caches are never cleared and are keyed by a name string

findings.title: Module-level loadable caches are never cleared and are keyed by a name string
findings.explanation: Both caches are module-level dicts that are written in examineFiles and never cleared, so they grow for the lifetime of the Slicer session and keep geometry dicts (per-frame numpy arrays) alive for every run ever examined. The sweep lookup is keyed by (filePath, loadable.name), and the name is built from series description plus run label, so two files with the same description and instance number would collide and the wrong sweep could be reconstructed. The comment shows the author knows Qt-wrapped loadables lose attributes, which is why the side table exists.
findings.suggestion: Clear both dicts at the start of each examine() pass, or key the sweep on the loadable object identity / a per-examine token instead of a name string.

items.title: Reconstruction runs on the GUI thread and re-enters the Qt event loop

findings.title: Reconstruction runs on the GUI thread and re-enters the Qt event loop
findings.explanation: FDK and SART run on the GUI thread and pump the Qt event loop from the progress and log callbacks. The modal dialog plus the BusyDialogGuard and the `if self.busy: return` guard in onApply limit re-entrancy, but any other queued event (scene changes, other module callbacks, timers) is still dispatched while a multi-minute reconstruction holds the interpreter, and a second Reconstruct click is only prevented by the disabled button. This is a common Slicer pattern but is the weakest point for responsiveness and re-entrancy.
findings.suggestion: Consider running the reconstruction in a worker thread (or at least a slicer.util.ProgressDialog with a queued abort flag) so the event loop is not re-entered from inside the computation.

items.title: Subtraction-run search parses the header of every file in the study during examine

findings.title: Subtraction-run search parses the header of every file in the study during examine
findings.evidence:
for seriesUID in db.seriesForStudy(studyUID):
                files += [f for f in db.filesForSeries(seriesUID) if f != filePath]
findings.explanation: For every candidate sweep, examineFiles calls _matchingRuns, which enumerates every file of every series in the study and, for each one that passes the cheap modality/numberOfFrames check, parses its header with pydicom to look for a matching trajectory. On a study with many series (or many single-frame XA objects) this makes the DICOM browser's examine step read a large number of headers synchronously, which can stall the browser. Results are memoised in the `summaries` dict within one examineFiles call, which limits but does not remove the cost.
findings.suggestion: Restrict the scan to series whose modality is XA/XRF/RF and whose NumberOfFrames is large, using the DICOM database before reading any header.

items.title: Testing/Python unit tests are not registered with CTest

findings.title: Testing/Python unit tests are not registered with CTest
findings.evidence:
if(BUILD_TESTING)
  # Self test inside Slicer (synthetic phantom)
  slicer_add_python_unittest(SCRIPT ${MODULE_NAME}.py)
endif()
findings.explanation: Only the in-module self test (DICOMCBCTReconTest) is registered with CTest. The 300-line unittest suite in Testing/Python/test_cbct_reconstruction.py, which covers FDK accuracy, Parker weights, the GE calibration fit and SART, is never run by the extension build, so regressions in the reconstruction maths would not be caught by CI.
findings.suggestion: Add a second slicer_add_python_unittest (or a plain add_test) for Testing/Python/test_cbct_reconstruction.py so the numeric tests run in the extension build.

items.title: CMake installs every imported Python file; entry and CMake dependencies agree

findings.title: CMake installs every imported Python file; entry and CMake dependencies agree
findings.explanation: Every Python file the module imports is listed in MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS and all of them exist in the tree (verified against the file listing), plus the icon in MODULE_PYTHON_RESOURCES. The catalog entry's build_dependencies ["PyTorch"] matches `set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS PyTorch)`, build_subdirectory "." matches the root CMakeLists.txt, and scm_revision "main" is a branch reference the index supports. The only uninstalled Python file is Testing/Python/test_cbct_reconstruction.py, which the module never imports.

findings.title: Catalog category (DICOM) differs from EXTENSION_CATEGORY (Reconstruction)
findings.explanation: The catalog entry declares `"category": "DICOM"` while the extension's own CMakeLists.txt declares EXTENSION_CATEGORY "Reconstruction". This is descriptive metadata only and does not affect building or loading, but the two sources disagree about where the extension belongs in the module list.
findings.suggestion: Make the catalog category and EXTENSION_CATEGORY agree (DICOM seems the better fit given the DICOM-browser workflow).

items.title: No network, subprocess, eval/exec, pickle or torch.load anywhere in the extension

findings.title: No network, subprocess, eval/exec, pickle or torch.load anywhere in the extension
findings.evidence:
import logging
import os
import sys
import traceback
findings.explanation: I searched the whole tree for network, process and deserialization primitives (requests, urllib, urlopen, socket, subprocess, os.system, eval, exec, pickle, torch.load, pip_install, download). The only hits are the GitHub URLs in CMakeLists.txt/README.md and the dialog's own `requestStop` method. DICOM input is read with pydicom (`pydicom.dcmread`) and SimpleITK, both of which parse data rather than execute it. No telemetry, no upload of images or identifiers, no credentials, no obfuscated code, and no text addressed to AI reviewers.

items.title: PyTorch installed only through PyTorchUtils, with user confirmation, never at import

findings.title: PyTorch installed only through PyTorchUtils, with user confirmation, never at import
findings.evidence:
if not slicer.util.confirmOkCancelDisplay(
            "Cone-beam reconstruction needs PyTorch, which is not installed yet.\n\n"
            "Install it now with the PyTorch extension? It selects the CPU or CUDA build for "
            "this computer and can take several minutes."):
        return False
findings.explanation: PyTorch is obtained only through Slicer's PyTorch extension: `import PyTorchUtils` then `PyTorchUtils.PyTorchUtilsLogic().installTorch(askConfirmation=False)` after an explicit user confirmation, and the catalog entry lists PyTorch in build_dependencies while CMakeLists.txt sets `EXTENSION_DEPENDS PyTorch`. There is no pip_install, no torch pin, no index URL, and no numpy/scipy/SimpleITK/pydicom pinning anywhere in the tree. Installation happens only when a user loads a run, never at import or startup.

items.title: catalog scm_revision is a branch name (main), not a fixed commit

findings.title: catalog scm_revision is a branch name (main), not a fixed commit
findings.explanation: The catalog entry pins scm_revision to "main", so the built code can change without a catalog update. The reviewed source is commit fdc8d856a39562bd282e1d204896297b070ec05f per the request, but the index will build whatever main points to. Policy accepts branch references, so this is informational only.
findings.suggestion: Pin scm_revision to the reviewed commit hash in future updates so that approvals cover the exact code.
